text: The service Pipit-4 takes traffic on port 5484, and the port is fixed across every environment. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Merlin-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Lark-5 is the Prism team. Nobody should assume the owner of Lark-5 applies to Merlin-8, the owner differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The primary datacenter of Merlin-8 is Lima; failover is handled by operations.
Finance fixed the budget of Lark-5 at $1605k, reviewed every quarter.
Merlin-8 reaches its retirement date on December 18, 2028, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
The primary datacenter of Bittern-9 is Hanoi; failover is handled by operations.
Lark-5 reaches its retirement date on August 19, 2027, so every consumer has to migrate before then.

Unlike Pipit-4, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Merlin-8 is 8033. Nobody should assume the port of Merlin-8 applies to Pipit-4, the port differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Egret-3 has one owner, the Lattice team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Bittern-9, which is 1700 requests per minute.
Source for Pipit-4 is written in Rust; no other language is allowed in its repository.
Unlike Bittern-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Pipit-4 is $2575k. Nobody should assume the budget of Pipit-4 applies to Bittern-9, the budget differs.

Unlike Merlin-8, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Pipit-4 is August 8, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Pipit-4 applies to Merlin-8, the retirement date differs.

Unlike Lark-5, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Osprey-2 is July 26, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Osprey-2 applies to Lark-5, the retirement date differs.
Questions about Bittern-9 start with its owner, the Sprocket team; they triage anything filed against it.
The service Osprey-2 takes traffic on port 8132, and the port is fixed across every environment.
The service Lark-5 takes traffic on port 2584, and the port is fixed across every environment. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Egret-3, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Merlin-8 is the Lattice team. Nobody should assume the owner of Merlin-8 applies to Egret-3, the owner differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
The retirement date for Bittern-9 is February 15, 2029; after that day it stops serving. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Pipit-4 has one owner, the Tessera team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Osprey-2, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Egret-3 is Priya Fairbanks. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Egret-3 applies to Osprey-2, the pager rotation differs.

Unlike Merlin-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Egret-3 is the Oslo datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Egret-3 applies to Merlin-8, the datacenter differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Egret-3 is implemented in Swift; the language was chosen for its tooling. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Egret-3, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Osprey-2 is Go. Nobody should assume the language of Osprey-2 applies to Egret-3, the language differs.
Finance fixed the budget of Egret-3 at $805k, reviewed every quarter.
The rate limit of Merlin-8 is 2950 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Pages from Osprey-2 land on the pager rotation of Gideon Nakamura before anyone else. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Bittern-9 was granted a budget of $3255k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
Osprey-2 runs in the Lisbon datacenter, next to its database.
Unlike Egret-3, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Lark-5 is Haskell. Nobody should assume the language of Lark-5 applies to Egret-3, the language differs.
